proposed_comments.title: Keep the haptic edge window hidden until a wrap is pending
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the haptic edge window hidden until a wrap is pending

**Severity:** high

The new edge-trigger windows are created topmost and left visible for the whole hook lifetime, so ordinary pointer movement at the virtual edge can still be hit-tested by the haptic overlay instead of the real application shell. This makes the callback-dependent route stateful for every edge pixel instead of only for an actual pending wrap. Keep the haptic window hidden until m_hasPendingWrap is set, and clear the pending state when haptics are unavailable or the message path is missed.

proposed_comments.title: Route haptic wrapping from device and monitor topology, not the virtual edge rectangle
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** CursorWrap::InitializeHaptics, CursorWrap::TryDeferWrapToHapticEdgeWindow, CursorWrap::RegisterHapticEdgeWindows, and CursorWrap::CompletePendingHapticWrap in src/modules/MouseUtils/CursorWrap/dllmain.cpp.

**Problem:** The haptic wrap path samples device state once during listener startup, builds its haptic edge window from the virtual-screen bounds, and depends on a later WM_MOUSEMOVE to finish the deferred wrap. In staggered, indented, or disconnected monitor layouts, the current logic can treat a real edge as missing, ignore a reconnecting device, or leave the pending wrap stuck while the haptic overlay remains visible.

**Why it matters:** Cursor Wrap should preserve the user’s configured wrap behavior even when display topology changes, the haptic device is hot-plugged, or the window-move notification is delayed. Right now the overlay can silently skip the wrap or leave the cursor stuck behind the shell message path.

**Suggested change:** Refresh the haptic device state from the existing display/device notification path and clear any pending wrap when haptics become unavailable. Build the haptic input window from the actual monitor edge segments that the wrap algorithm uses, and add a short timeout/fallback so a missed WM_MOUSEMOVE still completes the pending cursor move without relying solely on the overlay message.

**Verification:** Rebuild the exact upstream head and confirm the wrap still completes on a multi-monitor layout with a disconnected or reconnected haptic device, while ordinary non-wrap edge movement still reaches the underlying app or shell without staying under the layered haptic window.
